test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Indian National Satellites System (INSAT)?

options.text: They were designed for weather prediction purposes.
European launch vehicles have been used for the INSAT series.
They were designed for communications purposes.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian National Satellites System (INSAT) was designed for both weather prediction and communications purposes.
 
• The INSAT series was actually initiated in 1983, not 1979.
 
• European launch vehicles, such as those from the European Space Agency (ESA), have indeed been used for launching some of the INSAT series satellites.
 
• INSAT satellites play a crucial role in telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and search and rescue operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Satellites System (INSAT)**

 
 
• INSAT is a series of multipurpose geostationary satellites commissioned by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to cater to telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and search and rescue operations.
 
• The system was established in 1983 with the launch of INSAT-1B and has since been a key element in India's space program.
 
• INSAT satellites are equipped with transponders in various frequency bands such as C-band, Extended C-band, Ku-band, and S-band for different applications including TV broadcasting, telecommunication, and weather forecasting.
 
• The INSAT system also includes payloads for meteorological observations, which provide essential data for weather prediction, disaster warning, and climate research.
 
 
 
• **European Launch Vehicles**
 
 
• India has used European launch vehicles, such as the Ariane series provided by Arianespace, a European launch service provider, for deploying several of its satellites.
 
• The collaboration with European launch vehicles has been crucial for India, especially in the earlier stages of its satellite launch program before the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) developed its own heavy-lift launch capabilities.
 
• This collaboration has facilitated the successful deployment of various INSAT satellites, contributing to the robustness of India's satellite communication and meteorological services.
